name: Managing Telephone Poles
description: Mr. Chanek's city can be represented as a plane. He wants to build a housing complex in the city. There are some telephone poles on the plane, which is represented by a grid $$$a$$$ of size $$$(n + 1) \times (m + 1)$$$. There is a telephone pole at $$$(x, y)$$$ if $$$a_{x, y} = 1$$$. For each point $$$(x, y)$$$, define $$$S(x, y)$$$ as the square of the Euclidean distance between the nearest pole and $$$(x, y)$$$. Formally, the square of the Euclidean distance between two points $$$(x_1, y_1)$$$ and $$$(x_2, y_2)$$$ is $$$(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2$$$. To optimize the building plan, the project supervisor asks you the sum of all $$$S(x, y)$$$ for each $$$0 \leq x \leq n$$$ and $$$0 \leq y \leq m$$$. Help him by finding the value of $$$\sum_{x=0}^{n} {\sum_{y=0}^{m} {S(x, y)}}$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$0 \leq n, m \lt 2000$$$) — the size of the grid. Then $$$(n + 1)$$$ lines follow, each containing $$$(m + 1)$$$ integers $$$a_{i, j}$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_{i, j} \leq 1$$$) — the grid denoting the positions of telephone poles in the plane. There is at least one telephone pole in the given grid.
output_specification: Output an integer denoting the value of $$$\sum_{x=0}^{n} {\sum_{y=0}^{m} {S(x, y)}}$$$.
